q: Mercy file cleared for ruling-party donor without reason, probe shows irrelevant pick. What will court do?
options: Strike for mala fide under limited review
expl: Epuru rule: mala fide mercy reviewable on narrow grounds.
why: Mercy needs germane reasons. Irrelevant favour fails that test.

q: Same temporary tax law re-issued five times without placing before House. Challenge cites 1980s precedent. Result?
expl: Wadhwa: repeat re-promulgation sans House is fraud.
why: Ordinance is not parallel law-making. Bypass gets struck.

q: Head returns Bill once, House repasses unchanged, head still withholds citing discretion. Correct outcome?
expl: Return once only; repassage binds assent.
why: Single return exhausts doubt. Second passage prevails.

q: AP Bill on sensitive land issue reserved for higher head amid clash with central law. How to judge as aspirant?
options: Lawful referral when repugnancy or constitutional doubt arises
expl: Reservation is fourth option for clash cases.
why: Textbook rule allows upward referral. Avoid TV-debate conclusions.

q: AP Assembly has 175 members, cabinet lists 30 names after reshuffle. SI sees protocol list. Advice?
options: Exceeds 15% cap of about 26; needs cut
why: 175 needs max about 26. Thirty violates ceiling.

q: Why can nominated MPs vote for Vice-Chair head but not for top national head?
options: VP is MPs choice; top head needs states via elected only
expl: VP chosen by MPs incl nominated; President by elected MPs+MLAs.
why: Different colleges serve different roles. Nominated lack state mandate.

q: Why must temporary law die six weeks after reassembly if House silent?
options: To force House supremacy over shortcut law
expl: Expiry forces placement and approval; shortcut cannot persist.
why: Urgency justifies start. Only House nod justifies survival.

q: Claim: defector disqualified yesterday can be sworn minister today if CM trusts him. Extreme exception?
options: False, barred till re-elected or term ends
expl: 91st bar blocks minister post till fresh mandate.
why: Oath cannot cure disqualification. Re-election alone cleans.

q: Claim: top head can keep Bill pending forever and need never choose assent or return. Extreme case?
options: False, must pick lawful course; indefinite sit not envisaged
expl: Must assent, withhold or return once; no indefinite pocket licence.
why: Inaction is not a listed power. Delay cannot equal veto.

q: Link elected-only college plus return-once plus six-week death plus mala fide review. Grand idea?
options: All chain executive to elected Houses and reason
expl: Each rule ties head to House advice, time and reasons.
why: Election base, single return, expiry, review all curb personal rule.
